'''Julian Ernst Besag''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (26 March 1945 – 6 August 2010) was a British [[statistician]] known chiefly for his work in [[spatial statistics]] (including its applications to [[epidemiology]], [[image analysis]] and [[agricultural science]]), and [[Bayesian inference]] (including [[Markov chain Monte Carlo]] algorithms).

== Early life and education ==
Besag was born in [[Loughborough]] and was educated at [[Loughborough Grammar School]]. He began studying [[engineering]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] but moved to the [[University of Birmingham]] to study statistics, obtaining his [[BSc]] in 1968.

== Career ==
He then spent a year as a [[research assistant]] to [[Maurice Bartlett]] at the [[University of Oxford]] before obtaining a [[lectureship]] at the [[University of Liverpool]]. Inspired by [[John Tukey]], he visited Princeton for a year.

He moved to the [[University of Durham]] in 1975, where he became a professor in 1986. He was a visiting professor at the [[University of Washington]] in Seattle during 1989–90 and, after a year at [[Newcastle University]], returned to Seattle long-term. He officially retired in 2007 but remained an [[emeritus]] professor. At his death in 2010 he was also a [[visiting professor]] at the Universities of [[University of Bath|Bath]] and [[University of Bristol|Bristol]].

Besag was an [[ISI highly cited researcher]]; his 1986 paper "On the Statistical Analysis of Dirty Pictures" was the most cited paper by a UK mathematical scientist in the 1980s. The [[Royal Statistical Society]] awarded him its [[Guy Medal]] in Silver in 1983 for his contributions to spatial statistics, and he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2004.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Diggle|first1=Peter J.|last2=Green|first2=Peter J.|last3=Silverman|first3=Bernard W.|date=28 March 2018|title=Julian Ernst Besag. 26 March 1945–6 August 2010|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|language=en|volume=64|pages=27–50|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2017.0039|issn=0080-4606|doi-access=free|arxiv=1711.10262}}</ref>

== Notable contributions ==

=== Spatial statistics ===
For an array of random variables Y<sub>ij</sub>, [[stochastic dependence]] was known to be important. Julian initially researched a model to for the correlation between Y<sub>ij</sub> pairs as a function of the distance between the corresponding lattice point pairs. However, this proved to be difficult due to ambiguous conditions for self-consistency.

He therefore suggested using multivariate distributions for such a variable, taking inspiration from statistical physics and unpublished work by Peter Clifford and [[John Hammersley]]:<ref name=":0" />

<math>P[Y_{i,j}|Y_{k,l}:(k,l)\neq(i,j)]</math>

He published his findings to the Royal Statistical Society in March 1974.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Besag|first=Julian|date=1974|title=Spatial Interaction and the Statistical Analysis of Lattice Systems|url=https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.2517-6161.1974.tb00999.x|journal=Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B |language=en|volume=36|issue=2|pages=192–225|doi=10.1111/j.2517-6161.1974.tb00999.x|issn=2517-6161|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Death ==
Besag died in Bristol, 2010 following a surgery.<ref name=":0" />
